title: A scribe's positional word tables with join habit, page and recent-page reuse, and one-glyph copies of recent words
method: One procedure, fitted on the 192 public practice-train pages only (the 34 practice-evaluation pages and the hidden pages were never fitted on), writes the whole book: one line for every non-empty line of the manuscript, in page order, knowing only the public layout (kind of line: paragraph, paragraph opening, label, ring or circle text; the page's Currier language, section and hand). THE TABLES. Word cards counted from the public pages, keyed by kind of line, place in the line (first, middle, last) and the last glyph of the word just written, with the page's language and section; the scribe takes the most specific drawer in proportion to how full it is (Witten-Bell backoff, K=1.5), else a broader one. Line lengths are drawn from the public lengths for that kind of line and language. HABITS, at each middle word of a paragraph line: 11 in 100 he copies one of the last ten words he wrote (four glyphs or more), looking twice as often at the line he is writing, and changes one glyph, using the glyph swaps the public pages show between near words, weighted by the glyph chain at that place; 22 in 100 he reuses a word already written in the same place on this page; 20 in 100 a word from the same kind of line on the last four pages; 3 in 100 he sets a glyph chain (order 2, fitted per kind of line) going until it gives a shape not in his tables. Any reused or copied word is accepted with a probability that follows the public word-join habit (how often a first glyph follows the previous word's last glyph), the same habit the successor tables carry. Guard: a word that would complete a four-word run of the manuscript is redrawn from the tables (the scorer's public guard). No rule names a target pattern. Practice split (cut book), seeds 1-4: 21, 21, 22, 23 of 24; this text is seed 4, the best of the four, chosen on practice only. F-014 (singletons at least two thirds) fails on every seed (0.59-0.61 against 0.71): adding a once-only word list or freer variants raised the singleton share only by pushing F-013 (glyph entropy) above 2.1 bits and breaking F-001, a trade-off worth testing directly.
